entry.title: Asia Tech News Digest - August 29, 2026
entry.content:
# Source Title Summary Topics Link
1 DigiTimes Commentary: China's robot games offer Taiwan a reality check China's second humanoid robot games, held in Beijing from August 22 to August 26, 2026, sent videos and clips racing across social media and underscored how fast humanoid robotics is advancing. For Taiwan, the spectacle also highlighted both the promise and the risks of robots in policing, firefighting, and even warfar Automation Read
2 DigiTimes China's dexterous-hand makers take center stage as three technology paths vie for humanoid robotics China's humanoid robot industry is flourishing, and the recently concluded World Robot Conference (WRC) 2026 in Beijing revealed a notable shift in focus. Unlike previous years, when walking and motion capabilities dominated the competition, attention is increasingly moving toward robots' end-effectors. Automation Read
3 DigiTimes Qualcomm's HBC play pulls Samsung and SK hynix into a new race beyond HBM The AI infrastructure race has spent the past few years fixated on high-bandwidth memory as one of the most indispensable building blocks of accelerated compute. Yet as model sizes, context windows and inference workloads continue to expand, the bottleneck is increasingly shifting from how much memory can be stacked to AI Read
4 TechAsia If you can’t beat ’em, host ’em Why AI labs are hosting Chinese models to fund their frontier ambitions. Plus, we take a look at MiniMax’s revenue surge. AI Read
5 TechAsia Marvell forecasts Q3 revenue above estimates on AI demand Marvell’s shares fell more than 1% in extended trading after the results. AI Read
6 NikkeiAsia Robot from Japan lightens load of restocking New York grocery store Robot from Japan lightens load of restocking New York grocery store Automation Read

entry.title: Asia Tech News Digest - August 25, 2026
entry.content:
# Source Title Summary Topics Link
1 DigiTimes Samsung Foundry sees higher 4nm volumes as Nvidia ramps Groq 3 Nvidia's Groq 3 ramp is adding meaningful 4nm volume to Samsung Electronics' foundry business, with monthly wafer input estimated at about 10,000 and expected to rise above 15,000 in 2027. The increase comes as reported yields improve, Samsung's 4nm capacity remains tight, and pricing on the node moves higher. ElectronicsSemiconductor Read
2 DigiTimes GATE 2026 to spotlight Southeast Asia's pivot to EV supply chains GATE 2026 is set to bring together automakers, suppliers, and technology firms in Kuala Lumpur as Southeast Asia deepens its focus on electric vehicles, smart manufacturing, and industrial upgrading. The event's scale and timing could make it a key indicator of where the region's auto supply chains are heading next. Logistics Read
